newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $5 a tonne higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $5 a tonne higher.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $5 a tonne higher on Friday, in line with gains overnight in London, traders said.

London cocoa futures were firmer early Friday, but off highs, after an early attempt to clear 1,150 stg resistance basis September was unsuccessful. LIFFE September was up 11 stg at the midday break, to 1,147 stg.

Thursday, New York cocoa futures ended firmer, but well off high, in rollercoaster trading. September rose $7 a tonne, to $1,690, after ranging from $1,722 to $1,670. Spot July ended $9 higher, at $1,660, while the back months closed up $3 to $11.

On the charts, traders said Thursday's high of $1,722 in the September contract would probably provide some resistance, with a stringer upside hurdle seen at $1,730. Support was put at Thurday's low of $1,670, followed by $1,660 and then $1,654.
Fundamentally, Japanese Finance Ministry data showed on Friday that the country's cocoa bean imports in May totalled 5,073 tonnes, down 8.8 percent from the same month last year.
